generalfeedback:
To solve this problem we will have to use the method of integration by parts <hint>calc_int_methods_parts</hint> as follows:

Let \(u = {{CT:2}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:3}}d{{CT:4}}\) so that
\(du = {{CT:5}}d{{CT:4}}\) and \(v = {{CT:6}} = {{CT:2}}\).

Note that we can drop the modulus sign since \({{CT:4}}>0\) for all the domain.

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:7}} d{{CT:4}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:2}}{{CT:2}} - \int {{CT:2}}{{CT:5}}d{{CT:4}} + c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:8}} - \int {{CT:9}}d{{CT:4}} + c
 \end{array}\]

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
2\int {{CT:7}} d{{CT:4}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:8}} + c \\
\int {{CT:7}} d{{CT:4}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:10}} + k
